content.title: Vortex rings shape the feeding-efficiency landscape of jellyfish
content.abstract: Fluid flows enable and limit the feeding and locomotion of sea creatures across a wide range of scales. Although much is known about how microorganisms navigate life at low Reynolds numbers, the effect of inertial flows on the feeding-efficiency of larger marine organisms remains less well understood. Here, using jellyfish as an archetypal example, we study the trade-off between prey capture rate and energy expended to generate inertial flows by surface deformations. We develop a feeding-efficiency landscape that predicts an optimal feeding regime at the transition from Stokes pumping to inert
